faq.a: It is when the Sun stays above the horizon all 24 hours of the day in summer. It happens inside the Arctic and Antarctic Circles, because the nearby pole tilts towards the Sun.
asks: Where can you see the Sun at midnight?

faq.a: Polar night is when the Sun doesn't rise at all for one or more days in winter, inside the Arctic and Antarctic Circles. Around midday there may still be some twilight glow.
asks: Is it dark all day in the Arctic in winter?

faq.a: It is a line of latitude at about 66.5 degrees north. North of it, the Sun stays up for at least one whole day at the June solstice and stays down for at least one whole day at the December solstice.

faq.q: How long is a day at the North Pole?
faq.a: At the North Pole the Sun rises around the March equinox and sets around the September equinox, so there are roughly six months of daylight followed by roughly six months of darkness.
asks: Is there one day and one night a year at the North Pole?

faq.q: How do people sleep under the midnight sun?
faq.a: Many use thick blackout curtains and keep regular bedtimes, because bright light at night can confuse the body clock. Others enjoy the long bright evenings for hiking and fishing.
asks: Is it hard to sleep in the midnight sun?

facts: The Arctic Circle lies at about 66.5 degrees north.
At the North Pole, the Sun stays above the horizon for about six months of the year.
Tromso in northern Norway has the midnight sun from about 20 May to 22 July.

quiz.why: With the pole leaning towards the Sun, places near it stay in sunlight for the whole of each daily turn.

wrong.0: The Sun doesn't move towards any country; Earth's tilt causes it.
wrong.2: The Earth keeps spinning; the Sun just circles round the sky without setting.
